chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashab, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the sins of the visitor of Husayn (peace be upon him) are made a bridge at the door of his house, then he crosses them, just as one of you leaves the bridge behind him when he crosses it.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.) regarding one's sins?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to highlight the transformative power of Ziyarat al-Husayn, where sins are not merely erased but become a literal bridge facilitating the visitor's passage. This metaphor underscores the concept of *Tajrid* (shedding) one's spiritual burdens, reflecting the Shia belief that devotion to the Ahl al-Bayt serves as a means of intercession and purification. The imagery of leaving the bridge behind signifies the complete removal of sin's weight, allowing the believer to enter divine presence unburdened.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 30. It was narrated to us by Muhammad b. al-Hassan who said it was narrated to us by Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from al-Hassan b. Musa al-Khashab from some of his men from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

“The sins of a person who visits the grave of Imam Husain (a.s.) is like a bridge passing by. When you pass by a bridge you leave the road behind. Similarly, when a person goes for Ziyarat he leaves his sins behind.”
